Latest Update: What to Eat for Healthier Skin and Slower Aging

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2108 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • Recent findings suggest that on the quest to age smarter and slower, there’s a lot that your skin care can do.
  • To understand the connection between diet and skin health, Caitlin Hosmer, MS, RD, LDN, a registered dietitian and co-founder of MenoPantry, claims it’s important to define the notion of slowing down aging.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Recent findings suggest that on the quest to age smarter and slower, there’s a lot that your skin care can do. But perhaps one of the greatest contributions lies in the foods you consistently eat. Of course, diet and exercise are the pillars of good health, proper body function, and longevity, but a recent study done by scientists at the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) also reveals that 10 specific diets are linked to slower aging. Experts unpack the findings for ELLE and break down which foods you should incorporate or ditch from your diet to help improve skin health.

To understand the connection between diet and skin health, Caitlin Hosmer, MS, RD, LDN, a registered dietitian and co-founder of MenoPantry, claims it’s important to define the notion of slowing down aging. She points out that this particular DZNE study didn’t look at wrinkles or how old people feel. “It looked at biological aging, measured with epigenetic clocks. These read chemical marks on our DNA (methylation) that shift as our cells age. In about 7,500 adults, the researchers found that following any of 10 healthy eating patterns more closely was associated with slower biological aging,” Hosmer explains. The 10 eating patterns or diets included in the study results are Mediterranean, Nordic, DASH, MIND, and plant-based. Hosmer says that while the effect was modest, this kind of study indicates an association, not causation—proof that diet is the reason for the positive outcome—so it is still a meaningful signal.

Additionally, Mark Gilbert, nutritionist from The 1:1 Diet by Cambridge Weight Plan, tells ELLE that no single food has been satisfactorily studied and shown to be likely, on its own, to slow aging. “Of all the predictors of a long, healthy life, two of the best, which can be improved with diet, are muscle mass and strength, but this leads to a controversial conclusion,” says Gilbert. “The best nutritional intervention to increase muscle and strength is eating a high-protein diet. However, many scientists argue that high-protein diets have the opposite effect on longevity. So, if we can’t even agree on that, you can see that science has a long way to go to try and figure this out.”.

It has been revealed that one stat Hosmer found particularly striking was that over 70 percent of the biological pathways affected were the same across all ten diets. “I interpret that to mean that no single superfood is doing the work, and it affirms that [a combination of] food, diet, and nutrition impacts us on the cellular level. The foods these patterns share are what matter,” indicates Hosmer, who, along with Gilbert, breaks down the standouts:.

Alongside individual foods, Hosmer says certain diet components have the greatest impact on aging. For starters, protein is a must. “As we age, our muscles respond less efficiently to the protein we eat. This is called anabolic resistance, and in women, the drop in estrogen makes it worse,” she explains. Building and retaining muscle isn’t only about strength; Hosmer says it’s our largest site for handling blood sugar and a strong predictor of independence later in life. “Many women eat less protein just when they need more.”.

According to recent reports, gilbert adds that while protein is an key part of a balanced, longevity diet, there are some considerations to keep in mind before adding it to your meal. “I believe that because muscle and strength are so strongly associated with longevity and that protein, particularly later in life, supports them,” he claims. The caveat, however, is that there is a potential mechanism (which has to do with the amino acid methionine) whereby too much protein could have negative effects. “Many scientists argue that, because in insects and some other animals, less protein along with calorie restriction increases lifespan, humans would similarly benefit. Also, some cite the so-called ‘Blue Zones’, alleged to show that plant-based, low-protein diets are superior. In my opinion, all of these have been shown to be invalid,” says Gilbert.

Recent findings suggest that fiber is another essential nutrient that you’ll reap from plant foods and mushrooms. Meat, fish, dairy, and eggs contain no fiber, and because our enzymes can’t break them down, Hosmer says that fiber travels intact to the large intestine to assist. Once there, fermentable fibers become food for the gut microbiome; other fibers mainly add bulk and keep things moving. “As gut bacteria ferment fiber, they make short-chain fatty acids, which nourish the cells lining the gut, help keep that barrier strong, and keep inflammation in check. Fiber also steadies blood sugar and helps the body excrete estrogen the liver has already processed, supporting healthy hormone balance. Yet more than 90 percent of American women don’t reach the recommended 21 to 25 grams a day,” Hosmer explains.

Plant diversity matters, too, and not just quantity. Hosmer points to research from the American Gut Project that found people who ate 30 or more different kinds of plant foods a week had more diverse gut microbiomes than those who ate 10 or fewer. “That’s because each plant brings its own mix of fibers and polyphenols, and some bacteria have preferences, so a varied diet feeds a broader community of microbes. A broader community does more jobs. It makes short-chain fatty acids that protect the gut lining, helps regulate immunity and inflammation, turns plant compounds into forms the body can use, and even helps process estrogen.” The variety of plants Hosmer adds seems to matter more than any single “perfect” plant.

You’ve likely heard of healthy fats, meaning omega-3s from fish and the polyphenol-rich fat in olive oil. Adding these to your diet can support cell membranes and help settle inflammation.

It has been revealed that also on the list for Gilbert is vitamin D, which he says studies have shown to be inversely related to the risk of mortality. “This does not prove that low vitamin D is the cause, but it is compelling evidence. Although some results are controversial, low [vitamin D] levels have been linked to all-cause, cardiovascular, cancer, and infection-related mortality,” he adds. Vitamin D is intimately involved in immunity, too. It protects T-cell immune response.

Although Gilbert indicates, “The only thing all good nutritionists agree on is that there is no one ‘best’ diet or ‘best’ food,” he warns that for most people, minimizing the intake of sugar and refined, starchy grains and increasing protein intake is, in my opinion and experience, the best approach, but, again, different people can thrive on different diets. “As in the examples I gave, many of these foods contain phytochemicals—plant chemicals like polyphenols, flavanols, cyanidins, and others – which affect disease risk or support systems in the body that are likely to serve you well in old age.”.

In a recent development, hosmer notes several other red flags as contributing to unhealthy skin: Diets dominated by refined carbohydrates and added sugars, heavily processed meat, and regular alcohol. “Each of these drives the chronic, low-grade inflammation researchers call “inflammaging,” and blood-sugar instability.”.

According to recent reports, having seen so many gaps in these important nutrients in her practice, and understanding how women’s bodies change in midlife, led Hosmer and her team to build Menomix at MenoPantry. “One serving adds meaningful protein along with ground flaxseed and psyllium fiber, plus a range of plant ingredients. It’s made to help close the protein, fiber, and plant-variety gaps that so many women are carrying,” she adds.

To dive deeper into some of those gaps or bad habits that can send skin aging off the rails, Hosmer offers some eating patterns that push biology in the wrong direction:.

The information can be overwhelming, but instead of purging everything in your fridge, Hosmer suggests first focusing on adding good foods instead of restricting less healthful options. “In my experience, that’s more sustainable, both because it feels less like deprivation and because the “good” foods can displace the ones that speed aging up instead of slowing it down. You don’t need to pick the “right” diet and follow it perfectly.”.

Sources indicate that she highlights that the DZNE study found few people scored well on all ten diets at once, yet better adherence to any of them helped. What matters is the common ground. Mediterranean, Nordic, DASH, MIND, and plant-based diets vary on the plate, but they have a common core: more fruits, vegetables, and whole grains, and less red and processed meat, and added sugar. “That shared core is where I’d start,” notes Hosmer, offering this meal planning guide:.

Recent findings suggest that increase your familiarity with, and use of, plant-based proteins. Plant-based proteins offer an excellent package of beneficial nutrients, including fiber (not found in animal products). If you aren’t already familiar, learn how to include whole soy foods (tofu, tempeh, edamame) in your diet; add beans and peas and lentils to dishes here and there. Nuts and seeds and nut and seed butters count here also.

Build meals around vegetables and fruit. Fill half your plate with them, and choose deep colors like leafy greens, berries, beets, and cabbage-family vegetables. Those colors come from polyphenols, plant compounds that act as antioxidants and feed beneficial gut bacteria.

Sources indicate that make your grains whole and varied. Oats, rye, barley, brown rice, and whole-wheat bread are staples of the Nordic and DASH patterns, the two most consistently linked to slower aging in this study. Try a grain you haven’t eaten before—quinoa? Farro? Millet or teff? They are all cooked the same way—in boiling water, just with different grain-to-water ratios. Note: raise fiber gradually, with plenty of water, so your gut has time to adjust.

Count your plants, not your calories. Aim toward 30 different kinds of plant foods a week. Veggies, fruits, nuts, seeds, whole grains, beans, peas, herbs, and spices all count. A homemade trail mix, an interesting salad, or a smoothie with a handful of fruit and veggies can add three or four at once.

Recent findings suggest that choose your fats deliberately. Most of these patterns favor unsaturated fats over saturated ones. Use extra-virgin olive oil as your everyday fat, and eat oily fish two or three times a week.

Sources indicate that keep red and processed meat occasional, and keep added sugar low. Every one of these diets limits them.

Recent findings suggest that quality matters. Note that “plant-based” isn’t automatically healthy. A version of the plant-based diet built on refined grains, sweets, and sugary drinks tended to be associated with faster aging, as did a pro-inflammatory eating pattern overall. Food quality matters, not just food category.

Recent findings suggest that diet is the foundation the other efforts rest on. Collagen supplements and skin care can help, but they can’t make up for a body that lacks what it needs to build and protect tissue. According to Gilbert, collagen supplements contain very high levels of the amino acid glycine, which he says can balance the potential harms of proteins that are high in methionine.

According to recent reports, hosmer further explains that collagen peptides break down during digestion into amino acids and small peptides. Your body then decides where to use them. “To actually build collagen, it needs enough total protein, plus vitamin C. Vitamin C is a required helper for the enzymes that stabilize the collagen structure. It also needs minerals like zinc and copper. So a collagen supplement taken on top of a protein-poor, micronutrient-poor diet is not going to be optimized,” Hosmer states. “Collagen is also an incomplete protein: it’s low in leucine and lacks tryptophan entirely. It can add to your protein intake, but it isn’t a substitute for complete proteins when it comes to muscle.”.

According to recent reports, on the surface, what we eat affects the skin from the inside. Hosmer notes that polyphenol-rich foods and healthy fats support the skin’s own defenses against oxidative stress, and high blood sugar leads to glycation, which stiffens collagen fibers. The gut matters here, too. “Researchers call the connection the gut–skin axis. When the gut lining is healthy, and the microbiome is well fed, inflammation throughout the body tends to stay lower, and the skin reflects that. External products can only do so much if we aren’t supporting our skin from the inside,” Hosmer says.

Diet plays a major role in overall skin health and slower aging, but Hosmer argues that it’s not the full picture. To optimize more youthful-looking skin, consider other factors that may be equally as crucial as diet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

Who doesn’t love a good sauna and breathwork session to wind down the week? On Thursday, November 19, a group of estheticians, dermatologists, and friends of Cosmo celebrated our 2026 Acne Awards at Akari Spa in NYC’s Lower East Side.

Upon arrival, our guests were greeted by the lovely owners of the spa (and us, of course!), and swapped out office loafers for comfy slippers. Then we stocked the locker room with gift bags filled with Acne Award-winning products, hand-selected by our very own beauty editors.

Everyone got to go home with ANFISA’s Skin ÂN-DEW Azelaic Acid Serum, Sofie Pavitt’s Studio-Smooth Microdermabrasion Scrub, OMAD’s Bio Cellulose Masks, Face Reality’s Omni Clear Mist, Paula’s Choice BHA Liquid Exfoliant, Starface’s Salicylic Acid Pimple Patches, and Ultra Violette Unblock Screen SPF 50.

Industry observers note that and what’s a sauna session without a comfy robe? We provided custom ones from embroidery haven Abbode for each guest to wear and take home for their daily GRWM (and un-GRWM) routines.

Once everyone was bundled up, it was time to hit the saunas and cold plunge. Guests sipped on Happier Grocer green juices while sweating it out. Conversation about yoga and breathwork classes, skincare products, and wellness routines filled the rooms.

Upstairs, an even hotter sauna awaited those brave enough to break a major sweat. And of course, we stocked indoor and outdoor lounge areas for cool-off breaks with our latest winter issue. The night was a rejuvenating cycle of sweating, plunging, and relaxing ahead of the holidays.

The Watches of Grand Theft Auto 6 (and Their Real-Life Inspiration)

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For one glorious moment, the world appears to be united.
  • And amid all the fast cars, guns, nightclubs, and criminal capers, there's something else we pay attention to here at Esquire HQ: the watches!
  • In a recent development, rockstar Games' latest blockbuster reportedly features 34 "collectible" luxury watches scattered throughout its fictional version of Florida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For one glorious moment, the world appears to be united. Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived, to near-universal acclaim, with millions of people abandoning work, school, and presumably all their other responsibilities to explore the streets of Vice City. In these divided times, it's enough to warm the cockles of your heart.

And amid all the fast cars, guns, nightclubs, and criminal capers, there's something else we pay attention to here at Esquire HQ: the watches!

In a recent development, rockstar Games' latest blockbuster reportedly features 34 "collectible" luxury watches scattered throughout its fictional version of Florida. But that's only part of the story. GTA VI also has its own watch brands, although some of the designs look ... suspiciously familiar.

There's Crowex (a dead ringer for Rolex), Takio (distinctly Casio-adjacent), and Covgari, whose watches owe more to Audemars Piguet than the Italian-o jeweller its name suggests.

From gold Day-Dates to pocket-money Casio digitals, here are some of our favorite real-world watches that appear to have inspired the game's timepieces.

The gold Crowex is a near dead ringer for the Rolex Day-Date 40 (ref. 228238). The fluted bezel, black dial, and day window at 12 o'clock are all present and correct, although the bracelet differs somewhat from Rolex's iconic President. The Day-Date celebrates its 70th anniversary this year. Evidently, it remains the universal symbol of having made it, even in the virtual world.

The silver chronograph worn by a character overlooking Vice City has more than a passing resemblance to the mighty Daytona. The round case, contrasting sub-dials, and metal bracelet suggest that famous racing chronograph. As we know, the Daytona is one of the world's most sought-after sports watches, making it a natural fit for GTA's world of expensive cars, conspicuous consumption, and bling.

Industry observers note that brian Heder, a veteran drug smuggler, wears a metal sports watch that certainly seems to recall Rolex's Sub. There's the substantial case, dark dial, and the bracelet. The Submariner has been a fixture of luxury watchmaking since 1953, and its more ostentatious steel-and-gold versions would be right at home on the streets of Vice City.

In-game equivalent: Takio Digital Watch.

Jason Duval, one of GTA VI's two protagonists, wears a chunky digital watch resembling something from Casio's Pro Trek range. The large circular display, prominent buttons and rugged case certainly suggest its something from the range of the Japanese juggernaut. A more practical choice than the gold watches favored by some of his associates.

In-game equivalent: Takio Digital Watch.

Sources indicate that not everyone in Vice City is wearing a gold Rollie lookalike. The Takio F-BLAST is an unmistakable nod to Casio's inexpensive digital classics, particularly the bestselling F-91W. It has the familiar rectangular display, black dial surround, and simple, functional design. There's even a more colorful version, with a red case and two-tone metal bracelet, spotted in the game's Hamlet Thrift store.

As spotted by watch Instagram account @geesgshock.

Tech Report: I Am the Wildest Dream of Every Black and Brown Trans Woman Before Me

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (818 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As an influencer, a lot of times I'm the only trans person—or the only trans person of color—in the room.
  • According to recent reports, that’s especially true in this current political and cultural climate.
  • In a recent development, it’s been particularly challenging, too, as a trans person in the public eye; there's been many instances where my safety has been jeopardized.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As an influencer, a lot of times I'm the only trans person—or the only trans person of color—in the room. It’s a lot of pressure, and there have been times where I have anxiety before going to certain spaces because I will question "Do I belong here?" But I’ve learned that that’s just the patriarchy and society trying to make us feel like we're not worthy.

According to recent reports, that’s especially true in this current political and cultural climate. The trans community, especially the Black and brown trans community, gets so much hate—that’s why I’m very offended when people say being trans “is a choice.” Like, living with and navigating these stigmas and mistreatments isn't something that someone would willing choose.

In a recent development, it’s been particularly challenging, too, as a trans person in the public eye; there's been many instances where my safety has been jeopardized. When I get looked at, I'm thinking, They're looking at me either because I'm pretty or because I'm a viral trans person online. The differentiator is literally if I'm being chased home, which has happened multiple times. Since I speak out for trans women that can't speak for themselves, I'm also putting myself at risk. But at the same time, I think I can also make it safer for the next girl down the line.

Recent findings suggest that it's so rewarding being that person others can look up to. I love reassuring other trans women that they can do certain things or just live their lives authentically, loud, and open. But sometimes I'm like, Oh my god, how nice and easy would it be for me to just be silent and be in the background? But I don't think I was born to be a background girl. I'm front and center.

And I think that the trans women before me would want me to be. The hard work that those women put for girls like me now, I have to show up for that. I think about trans women on the front lines of trans rights, like Marsha P. Johnson or Sylvia Rivera—they were front and center at Stonewall. They were the voices for many then, and there was so much more violence. The community was pretty much hidden at the time, too.

There's so much trans history lost, and Trans Day of Remembrance resurfaces those stories. A lot of times things get pushed under the rug because trans people are seen as not crucial to the media, or people in general, especially after all the propaganda that's been pushed out by certain administrations. But every year on this day, I learn about a different girl, especially outside of the U.S. I’ve learned so much about how some surgeries started because certain trans women needed gender-affirming care, and they paved the way for girls down the line.

Recent findings suggest that education is the number one thing. I want people to know that your understanding of trans identities is not what you think and that there's a lot more to learn. There are times when I get frustrated because I see the stigmas and the rhetoric online that's really just misinformation, rumors, and lies that people make up about trans people. A lot of trans women have died because that ignorance can lead to trans violence. It's really sad to see. But we made it back then—and it was hard then—so we'll make it now. We're a strong community.

The trans community, we show up for ours (for the most part). There's a couple spaces made for Black trans queer people, like the Black Trans Kitchen by Queen Jean—it’s really beautiful. And Gia Love created the annual Celebration of Black Trans Women Cookout. Trans women that make spaces like that really inspire me because they remind our community that we matter. And we as trans people need spaces where we can just be ourselves, and really show care to one another. Those spaces not only keep me humble, but also remind me of everything I've been through. It makes me feel so grateful and privileged to be alive today because a lot of girls don't make it.

With the work that I do and everything I create, I want other trans women to see me and know that they belong and that they can be in those spaces too. I want to see more, especially more trans women of color, in positions of power and in rooms where you rarely ever see them.

I hope other trans women see that they can be their most authentic self, and that they can feel confident regardless of what anybody states. If you believe you're an amazing, beautiful person, it will reflect on the outside. I want people to feel that way and do that inner work because it's vital, especially for our survival as trans people.

Here’s how to tune in for the last season of Yellowjackets.

Latest Update: What’s in Her Pockets? Gemma Chan Kept Snacks in Her Pink Valentino Dress at the Oscars

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2006 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, gemma Chan first gained our attention in Crazy Rich Asians in 2018, stealing the screen as the glamorous, composed socialite Astrid.
  • In a recent development, now Chan wants to produce films, to spend more time in the creative process leading up to filming.
  • Recent findings suggest that this summer, Chan also starred in Peacock’s show of the summer, Five Star Weekend, based on the novel by Elin Hilderbrand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, gemma Chan first gained our attention in Crazy Rich Asians in 2018, stealing the screen as the glamorous, composed socialite Astrid. Chan imbued this character with a compelling emotional depth beneath the stoic exterior, a skill she honed during years of stage performance and her starring role in the British sci-fi show Humans.

In a recent development, now Chan wants to produce films, to spend more time in the creative process leading up to filming. Her first film, Josephine, which she also stars in, is out on November 20. Directed by Beth de Araújo, the movie orbits around the titular Josephine, an eight-year-old girl played by the scene-stealing poppet Mason Reeves, and her parents, Claire (Chan) and Damien (Channing Tatum). One morning, when Josephine is running through the woods with her father, she witnesses a rape in the park before her father manages to intervene and save the woman. Josephine grapples with emotions and trauma she doesn’t understand, as her parents desperately try to provide care in opposing ways. Chan delivers a deeply intimate performance, drawing inspiration from the inner strength of the women in her family.

Recent findings suggest that this summer, Chan also starred in Peacock’s show of the summer, Five Star Weekend, based on the novel by Elin Hilderbrand. She joined an all-star cast including Chloë Sevigny, Regina Hall, Jennifer Garner, and D’Arcy Carden. It tells the story of Hollis Shaw (Garner), a recent widow who decides to invite four friends from different stages of her life to her home in Nantucket for a luxurious, healing weekend.

Harper’s Bazaar’s questionnaire series “First, Now, Next” dives into the past, present, and future of some of our favorite creatives, spotlighting the moments and people that have influenced them. We touched base with Chan ahead of Jospehine’s release to talk about working with Channing Tatum, her time in Los Angeles unsuccessfully auditioning for pilots, and her dreams of running a cat sanctuary.

I would say the first film that I watched multiple times was The Sound of Music. We first watched it as a family when I was four years old. I would be imagining myself as one of the Von Trapp children and thought Christopher Plummer was amazing. He’s this terrifying but sophisticated guy who’s standing up to fascism. What’s not to like about that? Later in life, I would say the film that really spoke to me and made me want to become a storyteller was Secrets and Lies by Mike Leigh. What he managed to do there, and the emotional truth that his performers gave, was just extraordinary.

I was really fortunate that one of my first jobs was Secret Diary of a Call Girl. I met some people who are still my very good friends—Billie Piper and Lily James, as well as the director, Wayne Yip, British-Chinese like myself. The four of us became really fast friends, and we’re close to this day. It’s been a solace to have really solid friends from such an early stage in the industry.

It has been revealed that A key one was in the early 2010s, when I first started going to Los Angeles for pilot season and auditioning for a whole bunch of American network shows. I got pretty close on a few, and I tested for some, but I never landed one. The whole trajectory of my life would have been different if I booked one of those jobs. I went back to the U.K., and I did more theater and more British TV. I ended up doing a show called Humans, which I absolutely loved, and I would say that was a pretty key point.

Sources indicate that later in my career, it’s been a little harder to find roles since turning 40. It’s part of the reason why I have loved starting to produce and being part of the creative process much earlier and finding the stories and getting to work on something like Josephine, which I also produced.

It has been revealed that some of them are really, really fun. They ran the whole gamut, from outright multi-cam sitcom to procedural drama. It was crazy, doing six auditions a day, driving all over town, having to memorize 10 pages for each. It was a real task. You get to the room and look around, and you’re one of however many actors sitting there, and everyone’s eyeing each other up. There was one audition that I went to and was waiting. I’d been up all night learning these lines, and I could literally hear the casting director offering the job on the phone to another actor who had been there earlier that day. I thought, “Oh my God, what am I doing?”.

It has been revealed that when I was 16, success meant losing my virginity, finding a way to stay out all night without my parents knowing, and getting a bit of distance from them. Nowadays, success looks like managing to have a good night’s sleep—getting eight hours—staying hydrated, and finding a way to spend as much time as possible with my parents. I want to spend every moment when I’m back at home in London.

Recent findings suggest that there are a couple of things. They would constantly be on me about the importance of education and, eye roll, “I get it.” I am now the person who does that to my nephews, my little cousins: “Stay in school, kids!” Then, my dad had this particular way of loading the dishwasher. I’d say, “What are you talking about? There is no correct way!” I’ve discovered there is a correct way.

Recent findings suggest that I was first sent the script back in 2019, and from the moment that I read it, I couldn’t get it out of my head. The truth sang from every page. I had a meeting with Beth, and she articulated her vision and what she wanted to do. I thought it was so unusual and daring and audacious. I believed in her vision. Then the pandemic happened. We were going to shoot it, and then the strikes happened. It’s been a really winding road, and it feels like a small miracle that we finally managed to get it made.

In a recent development, for me, the character of Claire really resonated. I’ve been fortunate enough to do so many different things in my career, but I’ve never gotten to play a role like hers. I saw a lot of myself in her. I see a lot of my own mother in her; my sister too. She has this real emotional intuition, and she’s not the loudest voice in the room, but she has the inner core of strength. She’s a survivor. Getting to play her was an amazing challenge of stripping everything back and getting to the truth of the story and the script.

In a recent development, it’s interesting because Claire and Damien have been raised in different ways, and they’re carrying their pasts with them. It changes how they approach parenting their daughter. I would say at the beginning of the film, they’re a unified front and haven’t really been tested. Then this thing happens where they both deeply love their daughter and want the best for her, but they don’t agree on how to do that. The first cracks start to appear. With Claire, it was about going into her background. She speaks a bit about her own relationship with her mother, about how they never spoke about difficult things and she felt a real distance from her. I’d say Claire is someone whose instincts are right for the most part, but she doesn’t always follow through on them. I had points where I wanted to shake both parents and go, “What are you doing?!” But then, I’m empathizing with them because they’re just two flawed human beings trying to do their best for their child. There is no handbook for it.

According to recent reports, I’ve grown up and been a fan of Channing’s for a long time. If you think you know him from movies like Magic Mike and 21 Jump Street, you really don’t. What he brings to the role—the humor and the complete naturalness and spontaneity. He also brings such a level of vulnerability, and people will be really surprised by it. Before we started filming, Beth, he, and I spoke a lot about our own upbringings and our parents. He has a daughter, and that’s part of the reason why he was drawn to the script. We talked a lot about that and spent some time with Mason, who plays Josephine. We didn’t have to try; we could ease with each other. We hung out in the park. Channing and Mason got their nails done at the salon together. We went for dim sum. We did regular things, so she was comfortable. Hopefully, you believe in us as a family unit.

According to recent reports, it’s not in my closet, sadly, but if I had to wear one outfit, it would be the pink Valentino dress I wore to the Oscars in 2019. It had pockets. It had volume. It was comfortable. I kept snacks in the pockets for the ceremony. Bury me in that dress. It’s dreamy, and I don’t know where it is.

According to recent reports, the last thing I splurged on was a Steinway piano for myself. That’s amazing. Best decision I’ve ever made. Why didn’t I buy myself a good piano sooner? Something I will never spend money on is expensive mascara because you go through it at such a rate. You might as well just get a good drugstore mascara.

Industry observers note that that was a dream getting to work with those women. None of us had met each other before; we had a blast between every take. We’d be in our little huddle of chairs, sharing the hot goss, going right in. It felt really, really special. They’re a brilliant bunch of women. Regina Hall made me laugh so much that I peed myself a little bit on set.

In a recent development, people really responded to this show about women and female friendship. There’s no murder. There’s nothing to solve in that sense, but it’s just about their lives and the day-to-day. People really relate to that, and obviously you have the aspirational element of this amazing house in Nantucket and the food porn.

Recent findings suggest that gigi is diabolical. Let’s be honest about that. Obviously, you’re not meant to judge your character, and when I read the scripts and approached it, obviously I wanted to empathize with her. Hopefully, you understand a bit of where she’s coming from. Then I watched a little bit of the show and was like, “Oh my God, she is insane for going on this weekend!” Absolutely insane.

In a recent development, she felt on the defensive. She did fall in love. She never wanted to. She tried to break it off. She was pursued. It takes two to tango and, sadly, the other party is deceased. She has to take the entire blame for it. I hope that she’s not villainized completely. I feel that Becca, the writer, and Erin, the author, both wanted her to be a fully dimensional human being. Although there is that secret, she has a genuine connection with these women. She genuinely grows to care about all of them, including Hollis. That is not an act. She is a complicated woman.

Celine Song, Denis Villeneuve, Chloe Dumont. They’re all so talented. I’d absolutely die to work with any of them.

That’s an easy question! I’d open a cat sanctuary and rescue all the cats that I meet. I’m about to adopt another cat from Puglia. He’s five years old, and we’re actually rescuing another kitten that my sister found abandoned. She’s coming from France next month, and we’re going to introduce them, and hopefully they’ll get along.

As much as I love my 10-year-old bra-and-underwear rotation, it's nice to have a set that's sexier than the usual basics. When I came across this red babydoll set from Adore Me with the cutest red bow, it immediately caught my eye. It's festive without being over-the-top, and honestly, a much more fun addition to my lingerie drawer.

Recent findings suggest that but don’t forget, Adore Me has plenty of other gorgeous bras, sets, and rompers to choose from if you’re looking to add a little variety to your lingerie lineup. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to the woman who has everything (aka your mom, wife, grandma, or mother-in-law), the last thing she needs is more meaningless stuff. What she does need (and definitely wants) is something thoughtful that shows your love and appreciation. And now that it’s almost December, it’s really time to start thinking about the perfect holiday gift.

So what do you get for the woman who already has it all? Good question. Lucky for you, we’ve already handled the hardest part and put together a list of gifts any woman would want, no matter how full her closet already is.

Maybe it’s something romantic and personalized for your wife, like a luxury photo album filled with pictures of the two of you together; maybe it’s a flower or coffee subscription that will keep making her smile throughout the year. Or maybe it’s a latest apron for the home chef, a digital photo frame for the faraway grandma, or a cashmere sweater that will keep her cozy for years to come. You could even go all out and get her a sparkly piece of jewelry you know she’ll wear every day.

In short, whichever special woman you’re shopping for, there’s something here that will make her holiday season extra special, all thanks to you.

A pair of statement earrings for under $300 is a no brainer, especially when they look as nice as these suspended round-cut ones from Dorsey. If she wants something more dainty, go with the petite size; for something more bold, you can opt for the oversized version. Or keep it classic with the medium. Whichever you choose, she’s going to be impressed.

If you can swing a tennis bracelet that’s a step up from stainless steel and sapphire, it should be this one from Ring Concierge. With a choice of natural diamonds or lab-grown diamonds and 14-karat white gold or yellow gold, it is truly a luxurious and timeless piece.

A set of luxe pajamas from Petite Plume will give her the sweetest of dreams, and with more than 20 colors and patterns to choose from, there’s sure to be a set she’ll obsess over.

Made from vegan shearling, these fluffy slippers from Rothy’s are so cute and so comfortable, thanks to a cushioned footbed. Every day spent lounging around the house in these will feel like a luxury.

According to recent reports, it’s a small but mighty gift that lets her bring a reminder of you wherever she may go. Personalize it with her initials for a special touch.

If she’s astrologically inclined, try this made-to-order birth-date book, which features an illustration of her unique astrological birth chart on the cover and a detailed analysis inside.

The Dyson Airwrap is the hair tool every woman wants. With different options for different hair types and six attachments, she literally won’t ever need another hot tool for the rest of her life.

It has been revealed that everyone is getting into peptides now, and the best introduction to that is with Dr. Barbara Sturm’s upcoming peptide serum, which won a 2026 Esquire Grooming Award.

If she’s been talking endlessly about an upcoming weekend trip, you gotta get her the nicest weekender bag in the world, and that’s the Vérité weekender from Métier.

Industry observers note that don’t just gift her a perfume that smells good; get her something that will look good on her dresser, shelf, or wherever she keeps her fragrance. Bulgari’s new Omnia Amethyste eau de parfum is a gorgeous woody floral blend that comes in one of the coolest bottles I’ve seen.

Whether she’s traveling or just likes to keep her stuff organized at home, Afform’s Traveller is the perfect system to keep all her makeup brushes and products tidy. It looks so nice I actually keep mine on my dresser all the time.

A bottle of vintage Dom is for the lady who knows her bubbles. Like, really knows her bubbles.

In a recent development, so she’s looking for a new laptop? Make it the new MacBook Neo, Apple’s best-looking laptop that comes in at less than $1,000.

It has been revealed that nothing feels quite as luxurious as lathering yourself in Diptyque body lotion after a shower and before bed. This one has the brand’s famous rose scent, which she will fall in love with.

She’ll feel like the most elegant woman in the world lounging in this fluffy robe at home.

You can never go wrong with a diamond necklace.

When in doubt, go with something classic from Tiffany, like this 18k yellow-gold double-link bracelet.

Flowers are beautiful, timeless, and romantic—which is why they always make a great gift.

It has been revealed that for a luxury watch that’s especially luxurious, go with Hermès. This dainty silver Nantucket watch will become her favorite upcoming accessory.

If she’s a tea drinker like me, she’ll really appreciate a good tea gift set. We love this one from Forgrave, which includes black, white, green, and herbal blends and comes with the brand’s signature tea infuser.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Launching this week on Mr Porter is a 17-piece capsule collection created with New York’s own Thom Browne. Browne is famed in men’s fashion for his conceptual runway shows—staged in Florence, Milan, Paris and, of course New York—but beneath all the elevated showmanship lies a broad and distinctly wearable aesthetic.

In a recent development, consisting of casual and tailored pieces and extending to luggage, home goods, and even the recently launched Thom Browne x Bose headphones, the collection puts a youthful twist on Browne’s signature style that blends sportswear and suits with a rigorous attention to detail. Browne has acted as Chairman of the Council of Fashion Designers of America since 1923 and won its prestigious Menswear Designer award four times in his 25-year career.

Industry observers note that to showcase the collaboration, the capsule was photographed by Ian Kenneth Bird on young Fresh York restaurateur George McNally. If the name McNally rings a bell, that’s no accident; his surname carries a lot of weight in the New York food scene. George is the son of Keith (Balthazar, Minetta Tavern) and nephew of Brian (Indochine), both past masters of creating downtown Manhattan restaurants with an enduring buzz in a notoriously fickle foodie scene.

George—who, at just 23, has worked pretty much every restaurant position going in New York and London since he was a teenager—is tracing his own culinary path with Faux, his hot new space in Tribeca, serving reasonably priced, loosely French-Mediterranean food, and a space that stays open late for a city that, proverbially, never sleeps.

Go to Mr Porter to see and shop the collection and read George’s accompanying interview.

#89477. Latest Update: 12 Watches That Make a Great Gift for the Man in Your Life

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1319 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: 12 Watches That Make a Great Gift for the Man in Your Life

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1319 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A watch is a sentimental gift.
  • Sources indicate that but what watch?
  • It has been revealed that A classic watch for a classic guy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A watch is a sentimental gift. It’s not something casually given—not a tie or a fancy notebook or even a good pen or a nice bottle of booze. Don’t get me wrong, those are delightful things to receive and all appropriate for a run-of-the-mill holiday or birthday celebration. But some years aren’t run-of-the-mill. Some years require something extra. Some years are watch years—and trust me, you’ll know it when you get there.

Sources indicate that but what watch? It’s a personal choice, of course, but a personal choice that you’re making for someone else. Luckily, you likely know them pretty well. Around these parts, Esquire knows watches pretty well. Here are 12 suggestions, in price ranges from midwestern frugal to multigeneration inheritance. No matter how much you’re comfortable spending, you can’t go wrong with any of these watches.

It has been revealed that A classic watch for a classic guy. The Khaki Field Expedition is the quintessential field watch. Rich history of American craftsmanship, purpose-driven aesthetics, functional compass bezel (even if I can’t figure out how to use it for the life of me), and in the past few years it’s been available with the always practical NATO strap. It’s an ideal watch for the horologist, who’ll appreciate the history, the movement, and the exhibition case back. Win-win, guaranteed all-star gift.

In a recent development, I’m an unabashed Citizen fan. The Promaster “Fugu” is my favorite watch in the $500 range, and the Japanese brand’s Eco-Drive offerings are even more affordable. The Promaster Sea Eco-Drive is almost criminally underpriced for the watch that you get. We’re talking an emerald-green dial with a matching unidirectional 60-minute bezel, 200 meter depth rating, and a stainless-steel bracelet for well under $300. This is a great gift for the practically driven, classic dive-watch fan. And if the green dial is too swerve-y, the black and the blue are both excellent choices.

Good doesn’t always mean expensive. A big ol’ dive watch isn’t appropriate for every occasion or every guy. Simpler can be better. Like this under-$100 life-proof G-Shock. It treads the line between classic G-Shock aesthetics and little Casio reference. A watch equally appropriate for a man who never thinks about watches or one who is always thinking about watches—Schrödinger’s timepiece of no taste or good taste. And, hot take, it pairs better with a suit than sneakers do. Keep your shoes formal and let your watch carry the high-low combo.

In a recent development, if he’s not a G-Shock man, he may be an Ironman. A Timex Ironman, that is, even if he’s not logging an insane amount of weekend mileage. As the world grows wary of increased technocracy-driven smart designs, there’s a simple nostalgia to the ’90s-tech runner’s watch. Turns out they were right all along. You don’t need a phone on your wrist, just a stopwatch and an alarm clock and a 100-lap memory to boot. I also like the orange accents here. If he is midwestern frugal and would object to a gift over $100, this scaled-back version also plays.

According to recent reports, shinola’s Duck Watch references ’60s and ’70s skin divers, which sounds dirty but really is just a term for smaller, less depth-rated dive watches and the culture of free diving and spearfishing around them. That’s a reductive explanation that some watch nerds will quibble with, but it’ll serve us for now. The two important things to take away are 1) there was a magazine of the same name that you can find on eBay and 2) Shinola’s modern version is a killer watch. I have this one in Canary Yellow, but I recently borrowed the new Mallard Brown colorway for a photo shoot, and I love it. Hated to send it back. In the sun, the dial turns almost iridescent, like the titular duck’s feathers. It’s battery powered, water-resistant, and not fussy at all.

[Editor’s note: The Mallard Brown colorway is at the moment out of stock, so for the time being we will direct you to the Canary.].

Industry observers note that let’s get fancy. But let’s get fancy with purpose. More on Rolexes soon, but I think Panerai makes the most exciting watches in the $5,000 to $15,000 range. I realize that’s a large range, one encompassing the price of a decent motorcycle or a used Camry, but I’m talking luxury Swiss-made watches here. This is the tip of the iceberg. Panerai has design panache and exquisite movements, a design that’s not too “look at me” but still far enough outside the classic mold that it demands a second look. It’s not a watch for everyone, but man, those who will love it will love it immensely.

Industry observers note that recently I hosted a friend and fellow style writer for a will-not-be-named rival publication at the Detroit headquarters of T-shirt maker Soft Goods MFG. He had a couple enviable pieces (understated Nitty Gritty corduroy jacket, Paraboot derbies, perfectly faded vintage Levi’s), but I kept looking at his watch, a Unimatic Quattro. In the interest of individuality and my own love of a good suede, I’m suggesting this Todd Snyder collab as the next gift for that extra-special man in your life. It’s Unimatic with a twist, Italian design with an Americana POV, like spaghetti western for your wrist. Clint Eastwood fans rejoice.

Timex and J. Crew’s recent trout-forward collab watch sold out in an instant—unfortunately before I could get my hands on one. But there are other options for the outdoorsy dude. Especially one who cares about stopping forest fires. This Vero Smokey Bear option toes the line between campy and classy with aplomb. It’ll look good while you’re chopping wood or a little Wes Anderson–y at the lodge with a glass of bourbon in hand, telling stories about the trout that got away.

Industry observers note that TAG can get a bad rap in the watch-collecting community, but ignore the critics, especially if your intended recipient is a racing enthusiast. TAG Heuer has a long history in F1 and Grand Prix, and it looks as much at home in the cockpit of a fancy Brad Pitt–piloted car as it does in the fan stands or the sports bar. If you want to step it up a level, the Monaco is a luxury take on a race-day watch—all European angles and rich leather.

Sources indicate that this is the only pilot’s watch on the list—and for good reason. It’s the most handsome pilot’s watch on the market. Marathon developed these in partnership with the Kelly Air Force Base in 1986 and specced it out to withstand high-altitude flight, or even an ejection. If you’re in the market for a classic pilot’s chronograph, Bremont makes the best one. But if you are in the market for a no-frills, all-style, practically designed pilot’s watch, the Marathon Arctic Navigator is your ticket.

Industry observers note that maybe he’s a Rolex Pepsi guy, but you’re on a non-Swiss-made budget. I’ll let you in on a secret: Seiko makes a pretty damn good approximation. I particularly like that this one is PADI co-branded and automatic, with a 200 meter depth rating. Even better, it’s under $500.

It has been revealed that for my money, Doxa makes some of the most interesting dive watches out there. Is this on the list because I’d really love if someone took the hint and bought one for me? Hard to say. What’s easy to say is that the orange-dial Doxa Sub 200T is a showstopper. It’s got a slightly smaller profile and a more interesting silhouette than the original 200 but still retains the necessary details, like its unidirectional rotating bezel with its integrated U.S. Navy no-decompression limit table. No rules on whether that’s used underwater or just at the dinner table, either. It’s good to know how long to cook a steak for.

#89473. Do You Always Have to Sacrifice Passion for Emotional Intimacy?

Do You Always Have to Sacrifice Passion for Emotional Intimacy?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (904 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do you remember the beginning of your relationship with your partner?
  • Now, your relationship looks a little different.
  • It has been revealed that we’ve collectively accepted that a long-term relationship somehow means the end of passion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do you remember the beginning of your relationship with your partner? When you would be turned on by just the thought of your fingers sharing space with theirs? When you’d bust into the apartment movie-style, tossing aside layers of clothes because you just couldn’t wait to get to skin?

Now, your relationship looks a little different. There are no mental gymnastics before grabbing your partner’s hand and you don’t mind putting your clothes away nicely before jumping into bed. It’s a comfortable, cozy phase—one that you worked hard and long to get to.

But sometimes, you might wish you could have both.

It has been revealed that we’ve collectively accepted that a long-term relationship somehow means the end of passion. You spend months or even years learning everything you can about your partner. You’ve gained trust, a strong foundation, and yet, the passion seems to have disappeared with the uncertainty.

It has been revealed that “The comfort you worked so hard to build may be what’s subtly killing your desire for your partner,” certified sex therapist Dr. Mindy DeSeta, PhD tells Cosmopolitan.

In a recent development, she explains that over time, we unknowingly become complacent about romancing our partner. All of the exciting unknowns of the beginning of a relationship (Do they want to kiss you? Do they want to come home with you?) eventually fade away.

“You may be intimately familiar with your partner's moves after a number of years, and that's a beautiful thing,” Dr. DeSeta indicates. “But repetition can dull the excitement of physical intimacy.”.

But contrary to what we’ve all learned to accept, this isn’t an inevitable diagnosis for your long-term relationship. It is possible to have both emotional intimacy and sexual passion. You just have to work for it.

In a recent development, “Your sex life will suffer if you do not actively continue to learn your partner’s desires,” Dr. DeSeta says.

You might think that you know everything there is to know already about your partner. But as we get older, our desires change—even if our partner doesn’t.

“Your pleasure is constantly evolving and if you want to continue to have a thriving and exciting sex life, a couple must be able to talk about most recent desires,” she indicates. “What turned you on at 25 may not still turn you on at 40.”.

Sources indicate that this is why communicating your desires and feelings to your partner is so important. Sure, you and your partner may be pros at working through disagreements and emotionally supporting each other through life’s changes—but does that energy translate into your sex life? Do you share your curiosities? Do you hold space for them telling you they’d like to try something different? If you don’t, it might be time to make a change.

First, in order to feel sexy with your partner, you need to feel sexy yourself. Do something every day that makes you feel sexy and confident,” Dr. DeSeta notes. “The foundation of a great sex life starts with each person having a thriving libido.”.

According to recent reports, then try to initiate sexy conversation with your partner. Dr. DeSeta suggests planning something that feels tantalizing without the expectation of physical intimacy to follow. Reach each other erotica, talk about fresh fantasies you’ve had, discuss a trendy sex topic in media.

It has been revealed that “Many long-term couples need a prompt to get the sexy conversations started,” she claims. They also need reminders to touch each other more.

“Long term couples are notorious for forgetting physical affection,” she indicates. Dr. DeSeta emphasizes small touches every day. This can look like caressing their back as you pass them in the kitchen or holding hands while you watch your favorite show on the couch. Instead of maneuvering around each other, lean into the touch. It signals to your partner that you see them and want them throughout the day. And just the feeling of being wanted can ignite some of that passion from the early days of your relationship.

Most importantly, you should date your partner every day. Dr. DeSeta recommends “Daily Dates” to couples she sees in therapy. This is when you set aside 20 minutes everyday to make your partner a priority.

“All too often long-term couples put their relationship second, so this tune up is always needed,” she notes. “During these 20 minutes the phones are silenced, logistical conversations are off the table, and the time is dedicated to emotionally connecting with their partner.”.

In a recent development, by doing this, she explains that you slow down the daily hustle and really learn how to reconnect with your partner. You might even learn a few fresh things about them in the process.

Recent findings suggest that “If we do not make the intentional effort to keep the passion alive, then you are at risk of falling into autopilot,” Dr.Deseta claims. We often think passion and emotional intimacy are at odds with each other, but that’s because we think it’s acceptable to simply fall into our relationship without making an active effort to keep our relationship exciting. And no, you don’t have to be constantly ripping each other’s clothes off or feel nervous in order to have a passionate relationship. But you should aim to feel the same deep desire and attraction to your partner that you did when you first started off—if not more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you, like most people, hear the term “bourbon chicken” and have no idea what it is, let me call it by its more common name: toothpick chicken. Yes, the suspiciously delicious chicken shelled out at mall food courts on toothpicks is most likely bourbon chicken. Popular at American Chinese or Cajun-style Chinese restaurants, the sticky-sweet chicken is the utter definition of delicious, luring weary shoppers into food courts to find refuge from the bubblegum pink sweatpants and ripped denim. This version takes cues from the classic but swaps in some autumnal ingredients to make it fit for the season. Charred brussels sprouts leaves and pecans add bulk, while maple syrup and apple cider vinegar give it that delightful tart-sweet flavor we know and love. Serve it over rice or noodles or all by its lonesome for a hearty dinner that will take you back to the '90s.

More chicken dinner winners here: Sheet-Pan Hot Honey Chicken and Peaches; Basil Chicken Stir-Fry; and Ginger-Garlic Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry.

Whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, and ½ cup water in a small bowl to combine. Set sauce aside.

Toss 1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain, remaining 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, and remaining 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce in a medium bowl until chicken is coated; set aside.

Heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated, and cook, stirring very occasionally, until just tender and blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl.

It has been revealed that add more oil if pan looks dry and, working in batches if needed, arrange reserved chicken in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl with brussels sprouts.

Add reserved sauce to same pan and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove pan from heat and return brussels sprouts and chicken to pan; top with 1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped. Toss to coat in sauce. Serve chicken and brussels sprouts with steamed white rice if desired.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the first collaboration between the two brands saw them rework the hallowed A1000 digital-display watch.
  • According to recent reports, what about the APC-ness of it all?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, we’re in a great era for affordable fashion-collab watches. Timex is leading the way: its link-ups with Noah, Todd Snyder, and J. Crew are masterclasses in adding personality to classic designs without going OTT. But don’t count Casio out of the race. The Japanese giant has just followed up its 2024 collab with APC. The pair are perfectly matched: Casio watches are known for being beautifully functional and understated—adjectives that fit APC’s spartan aesthetic too.

Industry observers note that the first collaboration between the two brands saw them rework the hallowed A1000 digital-display watch. That release stripped back a lot of the original’s markings and added the APC logo on the dial. This time around, it's the AQ-240 getting a makeover. The case is squarer than the rectangular A1000, and while there’s a narrow window for a digital display, the watch maintains the traditional analog format with hands and hour markers. Here, you get the best of both worlds. The watch is sold out on APC's website but still available through Casio, so act fast if you want one. The silver variant is $110, and the gold goes for $135.

According to recent reports, what about the APC-ness of it all? That part is the opposite of loud: as with the previous collab, there isn’t much giving away the brand's participation. We’ve got the APC logo on the dial and the buckle, plus the brand’s guitar-and-dagger insignia engraved out of sight on the caseback. Casio already offers the regular A1000 in a bunch of different colorways, but these two new ones are made specifically for the APC collab. The release includes a silver case with a dark-green dial and another in gold on gold. Both of the pieces have a brushed sun-ray effect on the dial. The vibe is refined and stripped back; this is a fashion watch that almost feels anti-fashion.

Maybe the best way to think about it is as the reverse side of the coin to the excellent upcoming G-Shock 2500 Series. Both come from Casio, and both are minimal and functional. But the G-Shocks are big and bulky, with a design that seems to tip its hat to Patek Philippe’s Nautilus. These new ones are slim and nearly dressy. Put the two new releases together, and you’ve got pretty much all bases covered. And if those aforementioned Timex collabs felt a bit too classicist for you, then the Casio-APC partnership takes things in a more modern direction. Far from just being a cash grab, the “fashion watch” is now one of the best routes into affordable, on-point horology.

Jin Soon Choi, manicurist and founder of Jinsoon, describes the polish as a “crelly.” “The crelly finish combines the richness of a cream [nail polish] with the softness of a jelly,” she claims. “It gives this classic color a youthful, modern twist while keeping it soft and effortless.”.

It has been revealed that swift’s manicure fits right into winter nail trends. “We’re seeing richer, darker colors come forward: black cherry, garnet, burgundy, and deep wine,” notes Max Estrada, founder of eNailCouture. “They’re luxurious without relying on glitter or extra embellishment, and they work beautifully with winter fashion. It is the sort of color that gives a simple manicure presence.” Swift isn’t the only one—Jennifer Lopez and Anne Hathaway have both stepped out with similar manicures recently.

If you want to try it yourself, here’s how to re-create it. “Start with a clean manicure, shaping the nails short with softly rounded or soft-square edges and gently pushing back the cuticles,” Choi says. “Apply a base coat, followed by two thin layers of spiced red ‘crelly’ polish to build color without looking heavy. End with a top coat for an ultra-shiny finish that makes the color look lively and fresh.” And if you really want to nod to Swift, you can do it all while listening to “Red.”.

Steak Bites With Spinach Couscous

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A traditional steak dinner can feel like too much for a weeknight: too expensive, too likely to trip the smoke alarm, too fussy to cook to a perfect medium-rare.
  • More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.
  • boneless New York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A traditional steak dinner can feel like too much for a weeknight: too expensive, too likely to trip the smoke alarm, too fussy to cook to a perfect medium-rare. But cut a steak into bite-size pieces and suddenly it transforms into a quick-cooking protein that’s no more demanding than chicken breast or tofu. Rub the steak with the spices and make the quick no-recipe yogurt sauce a few hours ahead if it’s helpful with time management. To account for the extra liquid thrown off by the spinach as it cooks, the water-to-couscous ratio in this recipe differs from that often found on the back of the bag (or box) so measure accordingly.

More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.

Place 1–1¼ lb. boneless New York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp. dried oregano, 2 tsp. onion powder, 2 tsp. sugar, and 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl; season generously with freshly ground pepper and toss to coat. Let sit at least 10 minutes or cover and chill up to 8 hours (no need to bring to room temperature before cooking if chilling).

Sources indicate that heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or medium Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid over medium. Add 1 bunch scallions, thinly sliced, ½ cup finely chopped dill, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until scallions are softened, about 5 minutes. Add 10 oz. baby spinach in 2–3 handfuls, stirring and letting wilt slightly after each addition before adding more, 5–7 minutes total. Pour in 1 cup water and bring to a boil; season with more salt if needed. Add 1 cup Moroccan couscous and stir to break up any lumps. Remove from heat; quickly cover with lid and let sit 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over high. Arrange steak in a single layer; cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 6–8 minutes. Reduce heat to medium; continue to cook, stirring often, until meat is just cooked through, about 1 minute more. Remove from heat. Add remaining 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; toss to combine. (Residual heat from pan will cook out any raw garlic flavor.).

Industry observers note that uncover couscous and fluff with a fork to separate grains. Spoon into a large shallow bowl or onto a platter. Top with steak. Cut 1 lemon into quarters and squeeze juice from 1 quarter over steak. Scatter thinly sliced cucumber and some dill sprigs on top; drizzle with oil.

It has been revealed that combine 1 cup plain whole-milk yogurt and a generous pinch of kosher salt in a small bowl; squeeze juice from 2 lemon quarters into yogurt. Stir to combine. If sauce is thick, stir in water, a spoonful at a time, to loosen.

Serve steak and couscous with yogurt sauce and remaining lemon quarter and more lemon wedges for squeezing over.

Alan Krepack stands with his hands on his hips and takes a deep breath as he sizes up the Over Under: an obstacle with a high wooden box and low wooden beam spread 10 meters apart. Music booms over the speakers and other competitors shuffle around the cavernous room of the Armory Track in Washington Heights, New York, but Krepack stays laser-focused, thanks to years of meditation practice.

Recent findings suggest that as soon as the volunteer claims “go” he sprints to the box, plants his hands, and hoists his feet up and over. As he lands on the other side, he sprints to the beam, dropping down into an army crawl. “Take your time, take your time,” his son yells from the sidelines. Krepack reaches the far end, rushes back, and repeats the sequence again before crossing the line in 51 seconds. To cool down, he paces back and forth with his hands on his head. “I think I’m a sprinter, I’m a jumper, but then it’s like, fuck, no, I’m 73 years old,” he says, catching his breath.

It has been revealed that the challenge is just the first of eight trials Krepeck will tackle throughout the day alongside his sons, Harrison and Aaron, at the Super Age Games, a fitness and mental competition designed to assess abilities associated with healthy aging. On November 7th, the inaugural day-long event drew 530 athletes from 42 states and 15 countries, and about 70% of participants were between the ages of 40 and 64. Krepeck agreed to let me shadow him to understand this latest event through the lens of someone who is, in fact, aging, and would like to do so gracefully.

The name of the Games comes from a buzzword that originated in the longevity world: super ager. The term was originally coined by Northwestern University researchers to describe adults over 80 whose memories rival those of people 30 years younger. These days it’s thrown around on podcasts and in books to describe anyone who defies both the typical trajectory of both cognitive and physical aging.

The inaugural Super Age Games drew 530 athletes from 42 states and 15 countries.

According to recent reports, from crawling across a cargo net to reading microexpressions, the challenges in the competition measure longevity markers like functional strength, aerobic capacity, balance, and cognitive skill. At the end, athletes see where they rank among their age group and receive their “Super Age,” learning how their body’s physical fitness stacks up against the general U.S. population’s.

In an era where your average middle-aged midwestern dad is training for Hyrox, and a new, outlandishly extreme challenge is being invented every few months, the Super Age games are a low-key counterpoint to raw, stunty, athleticism, born from the metric-obsessed fitness subcultures who prize longevity above all. And now that fitness trackers like Whoop or Apple Watch can track VO2max, heart rate variability, and resting heart rates, that group continues to grow. Along the way, these stats have become status symbols on par with owning a Lamborghini. And now that overall health is quantifiable, fitness values have become less about just how fast you run or how much you lift, but how slowly aging.

Recent findings suggest that it follows that, despite its name, Super Age Games isn’t just for aging athletes. The crowd there leaned middle-aged, and the youngest person at the competition was 21. As we stood by the dead hang station, Krepak pointed across the room at a brolic young man who looked like he could be an NFL prospect: “That dude’s a serious athlete,” he says, as we watched him run around the track cradling a sandbag on his shoulder.

Unlike competitions like Hyrox, where athletes race through a sequence of workouts against the clock, the Super Age Games allows competitors to rest as long as they need between trials. In fact, Junior Kennedy, the fitness program director for the Games, encourages it. “There's no rush,” he states. “The goal is to get through each event as intentionally as you can. We need to understand what it means to recover.”.

Sources indicate that each trial was developed with a certain longevity marker in mind, and developed with input from researchers at the Buck Institute for Research on Aging, a leading nonprofit research center based in Novato, California dedicated to understanding aging. The Over Under, for example, tests agility by judging how fast you can change levels and switch directions. Meanwhile, the Synapse, a challenge where participants track moving balls on a screen and identify them after they've been shuffled around, is meant to measure cognitive processing.

Challenges in the competition measure longevity markers like functional strength, aerobic capacity, balance, and cognitive skill.

Krepack, a psychologist and lifelong athlete from Mill Valley, California, first heard about the event through its founder, David Stewart. Stewart is a media founder behind two niche longevity platforms, AGEIST and Super Age, where he writes about longevity, wellness, and redefining aging (one of his website testimonial’s indicates he has made aging “cool and aspirational.”). Krepack’s generally a skeptic of the profit-driven modern wellness industry—“I've always had a jaded view of all of that stuff,” he says—but he has followed both Stewart and the Buck Institutes’ work for years.

Sources indicate that the competition appealed to Krepack, in part because he’s spent decades cultivating a consistent exercise routine he’s proud of. He played baseball in college and has spent much of his life skiing, cycling, and playing other sports. These days, his schedule revolves around a handful of rituals: bike rides on Mondays and Fridays, a Saturday hike with a friend, gardening, yoga, and Zen meditation most days. When he signed up for the Games in June, he altered his exercise routine, lifted more weights, practiced hanging from a bar, and experimented with the Neurotracker cognitive test online.

Yet all that training didn’t prepare Krepack for the biggest surprise of his day. After scoring well on both the Inferno (the assault bike VO2max test) and Synapse, next came the fourth trial: the “Tightrope,” a balance challenge that requires competitors to walk along a low beam while carrying a water-filled bag, taking as many consecutive steps as they can in two minutes without falling. He had expected to excel, thanks to years of skiing and yoga. Instead, he struggled to keep steady as the water shifted inside the bag. As his foot slipped off the bar, his eyes got wide. “I can’t believe my balance,” he says. “That’s my one disappointment in life now.”.

Alan Krepack's sons Harrison and Aaron during the “tightrope” challenge.

Krepack was still hard on himself as we walked over to the dead hang trial. But after beating both his sons’ times, he seemed to get his competitive spirit back. He pushed through the remaining challenge determined to finish strong. And he did: By the end of the Games, he had placed second overall, with scores adjusted for age.

A few days after the competition, I checked in with Krepack to ask him how he’d processed the event. He responded with screenshots of his scores. His highest score came from the cargo net, which he credited to sheer determination rather than any particular finesse: “due to my will and overcoming an unconventional and desperate style!” he texted me, “Plus my sons were great support and focus partners.”.

Industry observers note that but the Games were also a reality check about aging: “I left there feeling both young and old,” he tells me on a phone call. As he watched his sons rocket through the obstacles, he was forced to confront how much of his athleticism he’d lost. “They just flew over it. They were so fluid, and so fast,” he indicates. “I’m not 30 or 40 or 50 or 60 anymore.”.

Sources indicate that despite all the longevity industry's promises of maintaining youth, Krepack sees little value in denying the inevitable. Aging well, he notes, is about “accepting, improving, and doing your best. It’s not a denial of who you are at this point in life.” The goal, he says, is to make the most of what you’re still capable of.
